In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WRR link scheduling policy outperforms FCFS in terms of delay performance, and the difference in performance between the two policies is more pronounced under heavy loading conditions.
WRR is the best link scheduling policy in terms of end-to-end delay guarantees.
WRR link scheduling policy is more effective than FCFS under light and medium loads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WRR link scheduling policy is more suitable for real-time ATM networks than the FCFS policy, and it can provide significant improvement in the network performance.
the FCFS scheduling policy performs better than WRR in most of the cases, and the performance gap between the two increases with the increase in the offered load of the network.
ATM networks can be made delay insensitive with a judicious choice of link scheduling policy and traffic description function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of an ATM network is not very sensitive to the link scheduling policy under light to moderate loading.
the WRR policy is a better choice for ATM networks with hard real-time traffic.
the end-to-end delay analysis in ATM networks is not difficult if the traffic is described appropriately and the network is decomposed into constant delay and constant delay servers.
